name: Modern SEO M1 L1: Modern SEO Welcome
body:
> Module 1, 2:11. Source: Lesson 1 Modern SEO Welcome.mp4

## In short
- The course runs over four modules and teaches the instructor's agency system for ranking local businesses, as step-by-step processes, not theory.
- Module 1 builds two skills: diagnosing why a local business is not ranking, and a repeatable process to fix it.
- The diagnostic process is called "the foundation of everything we do."
- The agency roadmap goes from a three-step foundation up to advanced strategies like the "Core 30 method" and geographic expansion.
- The three-step method (GBP audit, landing page optimization, super citations) is claimed to work for 70 to 80% of local businesses in markets under 500,000 people.

## Key ideas
- **Process over theory.** The promise is the agency's daily processes, broken into steps you can use right away, plus over-the-shoulder demos of a ranking method "we use for every client."
- **Foundational knowledge first.** The slide at 0:25 reads "We'll start with the foundational knowledge you need." Demos and frameworks come after.
- **Diagnose before you fix.** Find exactly why a business is not ranking and which changes would move it toward the top 3.
- **Phased roadmap.** Each phase builds on the one before. You move from basic optimizations to geographic expansion only when it is time.
- **The basics are often enough.** In smaller markets the three-step method gets most businesses ranked "reasonably well without complex strategies."
- **Beyond ranking.** The course also introduces the Core 30 framework and client acquisition strategies for agencies.

## Step-by-step process
Module 1 lesson plan as previewed (slides at 1:05, 1:25, 1:45):
1. "In lesson 2": the instructor diagnoses a local business website that is currently stuck. Slide: "My system for finding why a business isn't ranking and how to move it into the top 3."
2. "In lesson 3": the complete agency process. Slide: "The full roadmap we follow for every single client" and "From the initial 3-step foundation through advanced strategies like our 'Core 30 method'."
3. "In lesson 4": the 3-step method in detail. Slide: "70-80% of local businesses in markets under 500,000 people." The three steps named in audio:
   1. GBP audit
   2. Landing page optimization
   3. Super citation process

> The actual lesson files do not match this preview. The real Lesson 3 is "How Google and AI Actually Work," the agency roadmap is Lesson 4 ("How We Do Local SEO"), and the three-step method is Lesson 5 ("The Low Competition Ranking Method"). See Open questions.

## Checklist
- Diagnose why the business is not ranking before changing anything.
- Confirm the three-step foundation (GBP audit, landing page, super citations) is done before moving to advanced strategies like Core 30.
- Note the market size (under or over 500,000 people) to judge whether the three-step method alone is likely to be enough.

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| Core 30 framework / method | Advanced strategy for later phases and geographic expansion (not explained yet) | 0:35, 1:22 |
| Three-step method | Foundation process: GBP audit, landing page optimization, super citations | 1:20, 1:35 |
| GBP (Google Business Profile) audit | Step 1 of the three-step method | 1:44 |
| Super citation process | Step 3 of the three-step method (not explained yet) | 1:44 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
These are the instructor's claims, not verified facts.
- 4 modules in the course. (0:04, slide at 0:05)
- The methods "have generated millions in revenue for our clients." (0:09)
- Goal: move a business toward the top 3 positions. (1:04, slide at 1:05)
- The three-step method works for 70 to 80% of local businesses in markets under 500,000 people. (1:39, slide at 1:45)

## Terms
**Core 30:** The instructor's advanced framework, named here as part of the roadmap after the three-step foundation. Defined in Lesson 4.
**Three-step method:** GBP audit, landing page optimization, and super citations.
**Super citation:** Step 3 of the method. Defined in Lesson 5.
**Stuck:** A local business that is not ranking higher and needs a diagnosis.

## Worth quoting
- "This diagnostic process is the foundation of everything we do." (1:09)
- "I'm not going to go over theory or generic advice." (0:14)

## How to use this at TAG
- Treat the Lesson 2 diagnosis as the first step for any review of Pipeliners, Alphalete, or Summit AZ, before recommending changes.
- Use the three-step foundation as a simple frame to see which area (GBP, landing page, citations) is weakest for each client. Any GBP or site changes are Kim's to apply. Claude stays read-only on client sites.

## Open questions
- **Lesson numbering mismatch.** The intro previews the agency process as Lesson 3 and the three-step method as Lesson 4. In the actual files these are Lessons 4 and 5, and Lesson 3 (How Google and AI Actually Work) is not mentioned in this intro. Likely the course added a lesson after this intro was recorded (unclear in video).
- "Core 30" and "super citation" are named but not defined here.
- "Millions in revenue" and the 70 to 80% figure are unverified instructor claims.
- The "In lesson 4" slide at 1:45 has an empty third bullet box. Probably an animation still loading, not missing content.
- No low-confidence transcript lines.

## Timestamps
- 0:01 Welcome, four modules, process over theory
- 0:24 Foundational knowledge first, then over-the-shoulder demos
- 0:33 Core 30 and client acquisition introduced
- 0:53 Lesson 2 preview: diagnosing a stuck website
- 1:13 Lesson 3 preview: full agency roadmap, from three-step foundation to Core 30
- 1:33 Lesson 4 preview: three-step method, 70 to 80% claim
- 1:44 The three steps named
- 1:53 Module goals: diagnostic skills plus a systematic fix process
